notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 model with run_id ros-wave-c-125, reviewed_by stays null; no human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no MuJoCo engine, ROS graph, simulator or robot run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper RosDriver (family ros), but the pinned clone's MuJoCo path is the C++ mujoco_ros2_control node, which loads the selected MJCF as robot_model_path (single_go2w_mujoco_cfpa2.launch.py:281-291); that node exposes no ROS reset/step service or action, and the clone has no rosbridge deployment. The VLM launch defaults mujoco_model_path to go2_gazebo_sim/mujoco/vlm_exploration_scene.xml (single_vlm_mujoco_far.launch.py:142-146). The card's own candidate classes are cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1, its models list is a set of MJCF scenes, and its mock strategy prefers the upstream simulator. The card lists src/vlm_explorer/worlds/vlm_exploration_scene.xml as models[0], but the VLM launch binds the go2_gazebo_sim/mujoco/vlm_exploration_scene.xml copy; only that launch-bound copy is served, and the other MJCF scenes are NOT COVERED. The package therefore uses MujocoDriver over that launch-bound scene (model_path points at the read-only clone in place; it is not copied or modified). No Python native exists and native.py is not used. The ROS 2 control and sensor graph, Nav2, SLAM, the other MJCF scenes and the real-robot ROS 1 deployment are NOT COVERED.

WHAT IT SERVES: cap.world.step.v1 {ticks, action:{ctrl:[16 numbers]}} and cap.world.reset.v1. The selected scene has one free joint and 16 hinge joints, giving 23 qpos and 22 qvel entries, and 12 motor plus four velocity actuators, giving 16 ctrl entries; option timestep is 0.002 s (vlm_exploration_scene.xml:4). The bridge reads actuator_ctrlrange from the model: the go2 class sets -23.7..23.7, the knee class sets -45.43..45.43 and the four velocity elements set -15..15 (vlm_exploration_scene.xml:18-36, 361-381), so the reference shows those per-element bounds and the driver invents none. World state = time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed, native_checkpoint. cap.world.seed.v1 is not served by MujocoBridge; reset's seed field is accepted but mj_resetData does not use a seed.

SAFETY: risk R0 reflects isolated simulated world stepping (MHS-004 SAFE-006); no physical mobile-base command, actuator torque, sensor stream or hardware command is exposed. The runtime's software e-stop latch blocks step and reset until mhs.safety.reset, while state remains readable; this is not a hardware e-stop and makes no physical-safety claim. No estop_physical_ref is claimed.

FAKE: the fake backend is a package-local stand-in for the mujoco module, not the upstream simulator. It parses the MJCF and its includes for model shape, actuator names and ctrlranges and advances a placeholder joint state; it loads no mesh/texture/inertia/contact, resolves no friction/tendon/equality/force constraint, and uses the bridge's basic snapshot profile (time, qpos, qvel, act, ctrl; no full integration/warm-start). Fidelity is F0 with lockstep clock, no realtime pacing and the gaps listed in driver.py; the real sim backend would be the official mujoco module loading the same file, which was not installed or run. G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND are the SDK's simulator-family warnings for a class-object backend; they do not mean this fake is the upstream simulator and no native call recording is claimed. G8.NO_UNIT x3 (ticks, action.ctrl[*], seed) are expected for MuJoCo-derived world classes per PLAYBOOK.md section 8; no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were raised. The model has sourced ctrlranges, so no operator-required limit was needed.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds seven cases: model shape from the MJCF (23/22/16, timestep 2 ms, derived ctrl bounds), step applying ctrl and advancing ticks/state, reset restoring model defaults, malformed inputs rejected before state change, out-of-envelope ctrl refused before state change, e-stop latching step with state readable and reset releasing it, and repeatability of the placeholder state hash. All pass.

No catalogue_requests: only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. The clone was left unmodified (G1 passed); no network, pip install or upstream execution was used.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation (the VLM launch defaults to go2_gazebo_sim/mujoco/vlm_exploration_scene.xml, single_vlm_mujoco_far.launch.py:142-146, the MJCF the C++ mujoco_ros2_control node steps; the card's models[0] copy under vlm_explorer/worlds is a different file no launch selects), the model path and its OBJ/STL meshes (present), the derived shape (23 qpos, 22 qvel, 16 ctrl, 2 ms), the 16 sourced ctrlranges, all 12 facts, the stand-in fake and the lockstep latch, which does stop this in-process simulation. Defects: the stand-in reset every qpos entry to zero, including the free joint's quaternion, while mj_resetData restores qpos0 (base at 4.0 0 0.6, identity quaternion), and a test asserted the zeros; it treated all 16 controls as joint velocities although the twelve motor actuators apply force and the four velocity actuators kv*(ctrl - qvel), and a test asserted those velocities; three facts said more than their lines ('hinge', 'as its ROS bridge', a clause about the package on the sensor lines); the clone's licence notes and real-Go2 deployment were not recorded. The reviewer changed fake.py (qpos0 from the MJCF, force and velocity-servo placeholder integration), test_driver.py (qpos0 in the shape and reset cases, placeholder direction checks in the step case), driver.py (three facts narrowed, three added: the knee range, the README licence text, the MIT manifest; the README fact now includes the real-Go2 clause; real-engine gaps for the uncompiled scene, qpos0 outside the calf range with no keyframe, and ctrl persistence; stand-in gaps rewritten) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected MuJoCo-family warnings (G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, G8.NO_UNIT x3) and the digest unchanged (sha256:485dc5cfd8fafacfd1022d3c78f7e67fb1e823409f25c0cbe2c8f00baa6cf4ef); the author's notes describing the stand-in's placeholder joint update and its reset to the model defaults are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Simulation only: the package steps its own in-process MuJoCo copy of the VLM scene read in place from the clone; an MHS e-stop latches that instance only, not a separately launched mujoco_ros2_control simulation. The real MuJoCo backend was never run: confirm the scene compiles before sim use. The bare plant has raw motor torques and wheel-velocity servos with no controller, and reset puts every leg joint at 0, outside the calf range. The repository also deploys to a real Go2 (ROS 1 Noetic on a Jetson Orin NX, HIL scripts); that legged-hardware path is out of scope and would be R2 or higher. Licence: the README says 'Contact maintainers for licensing' while the go2_gazebo_sim manifest says MIT; publish_review required, the owner decides.
